title: Retainer-scale incident activation and external communications
author: Maya Patel
body:
Summary:
This playbook describes the process for activating an incident where we expect extended multi-hour customer impact that could trigger reserved-capacity/retainer engagement. It combines runloop steps for containment and recovery with a customer-facing briefing catalog and an evidence collection checklist to accelerate post-incident analysis. Use this when impact is: widespread (>20% customer error rate or SLO breach across multiple tenants), long-running (>30 minutes at scale), or when legal/compliance/enterprise customers require dedicated incident coordination.

Scope and intent:
- Scope: Redwood hosted endpoints, Dedicated pools, and Private control-plane handoffs.
- Intent: give a single, repeatable procedure for (1) rapid escalation to an incident bridge with retainer support, (2) consistent customer communications, and (3) prioritized evidence capture for postmortem and billing/contract reconciliation.

Activation criteria (any of):
1. Cross-region latency SLO breach > 2 minutes sustained for more than two consecutive 5-minute windows.
2. Multi-tenant error spike > 20% of requests or systematic 5xx increase for gateway/service mesh.
3. KV cache or routing-layer corruption causing incorrect outputs for customers (data correctness incidents).
4. Security indicators combined with service impact (escalate to SecOps immediately).

Quick roles (single-line reference):
- Incident Commander (IC): overall decision authority for this incident.
- Bridge Operator (Bridge): runs the conferencing bridge and triage canvas.
- SRE Lead: leads technical investigation and runbooks.
- Comms Owner: drafts external and customer messages; coordinates with CS and Legal.
- Customer Liaison: single point for enterprise customers on the retainer.
- Retainer Liaison: responsible for engaging vendor/supplier resources covered by the retainer.

Incident activation checklist (first 10 minutes):
1. Acknowledge and classify severity: use S1/S2 scale. If criteria met, mark as "Retainer Activation".
2. Create incident artifact: new incident channel (name: INCIDENT-{YYYYMMDD}-{SERVICE}-{SEV}).
3. Start bridge and set context: Bridge Operator creates bridge URL, adds IC, SRE Lead, Comms Owner, Customer Liaison, Retainer Liaison.
4. Snapshot key metrics and topology: run the commands below, attach outputs to the incident channel:
   - curl -s https://monitoring-api.redwood.internal/now?range=5m > metrics-5m.json
   - kubectl get pods -A -o wide --show-labels > pods-snapshot.txt
   - rtr snapshot --service $SERVICE --output snapshot.tar.gz
5. Apply immediate mitigations (if safe): scale up read replicas, enable graceful fallback to model-variant, and toggle rate-limiting to preserve core traffic. Document every change.
6. Request CS to assemble impacted customer list and map to contract/retainer coverage.
7. Draft an initial public status (see templates below) and confirm with IC.
8. Open a Postmortem ticket in tracker (label: incident-evidence-required, severity, retainer).

Decision ladder (who approves what):
- IC: approve customer-wide notices, major rollout rollbacks, and production failover.
- SRE Lead: approve technical mitigations and short-term config changes.
- Comms Owner + Legal: approve wording of public statements when enterprise customers are affected.
- CTO on-call: notified for critical cross-org escalations or when legal/regulatory exposure is likely.

Containment & mitigation runbooks (select based on signal):
- High error-rate (gateway 5xx):
  1) Verify circuit limits and service mesh health.
  2) If 90th percentile CPU or connection queues are saturated, throttle non-critical background workloads.
  3) If errors persist after throttling, switch traffic to warm standby pool and enable prioritized customer routing.

- KV cache corruption / model-serving corruption:
  1) Quarantine affected model instances: set maintenance flag on affected nodes.
  2) Invalidate KV cache prefixes (automated script below); monitor correctness checks.
  3) Roll forward to last known-good model version or rollback if a bad deploy suspected.
  Script: 
  ```bash
  # invalidate prefixes for service
  python tools/cache_invalidator.py --service $SERVICE --prefixes recent --commit-id $DEPLOY_ID
  ```

- Capacity spike / noisy neighbor:
  1) Activate capacity-eviction policy: move best-effort tenants to burst nodes.
  2) Temporarily limit batch sizes for interactive endpoints to reduce token amplification.
  3) Apply rate limit backpressure at edge for non-retained API keys.

Evidence capture checklist (high-priority items, automated where possible):
- Metrics and dashboards (5m, 15m, 1h windows).
- Service logs with correlated request IDs for affected windows.
- Traces for a representative sample of failed and successful requests.
- Deployment history and release commits for last 24 hours.
- Model versions and parameter/quantization profiles in use.
- KV cache dump (head and tail keys) and invalidation timestamps.
- GPU telemetry: utilization, memory pressure, CUDA kernel errors.
- Network path snapshots (BGP/peer status if multi-cloud).
- Pager history and oncall roster for the incident window.

Post-incident customer communications catalog
(templates — replace placeholders):

Severity 1 — initial external notice (short):
Subject: Redwood Inference — Incident affecting {service} (S1)
Body:
We’re investigating an active incident impacting {service} which may cause increased errors and latency for customers in {regions}. Our SRE team has opened an incident bridge and is working on containment. We will post an update within 30 minutes. If you rely on a retainer or dedicated capacity, your Customer Liaison has been notified.

Severity 1 — follow-up update (technical):
Subject: Update — {service} incident (S1) — mitigation in progress
Body:
- Summary of what changed since last update (e.g., "rolled traffic to warm pool; invalidated cache prefixes").
- Current impact: "error rate reduced from 42% -> 9% for majority of customers; some enterprise tenants still affected".
- Next steps and expected time to next update (e.g., 15 minutes).

Severity 2 — customer notice (non-urgent):
Subject: Notice — degraded performance for {service}
Body:
We observed elevated latency for {service} affecting a subset of requests. Our engineers implemented a short-term mitigation and are monitoring. No action required from customers at this time.

Customer liaison script (enterprise calls):
- Objectives: confirm impact, verify SLAs/retainer coverage, set expectations on timeline, and establish primary contact cadence (every 30m/60m).
- Script bullets to read on call:
  - "We’ve isolated the scope to {region}/{tenant subset} and have applied a mitigation. Our current estimate for full restoration is {ETA}."
  - "We will share a technical postmortem within 72 hours and make any contractual adjustments if required."

Status page guidance and cadence:
- Initial status: acknowledge incident within 15 minutes of activation.
- Update cadence: 30 minutes for S1 until containment, then hourly until resolved.
- Final update: resolution summary, impact statement, and link to postmortem.
- Status templates should include: root cause summary, affected customers, workaround applied, ETA for resolution, and next update time.

Postmortem and severity review process:
1. Owner assignment: IC assigns a Postmortem Lead within 2 hours of resolution.
2. Evidence upload: SRE Lead ensures all items from evidence checklist are attached to the postmortem ticket.
3. Drafting: Postmortem Lead drafts narrative using this structure: Timeline -> Root cause analysis -> Corrective actions -> Preventative controls -> Rollout plan and owners.
4. Review window: 72 hours for technical reviewers, 7 days for cross-org approvals.
5. Closure: postmortem published to confluence and linked on the incident artifact. If contractual remediation required, Finance/Legal and CS enter remediation workflow.

On-call rotation & retainer engagement rules (summary):
- On-call shifts: primary oncall (12-hour), secondary (24-hour overlap for weekends).
- Retainer engagement: if customer has an active retainer, Customer Liaison must be looped in within first 10 minutes. Retainer resources can be requested by the IC; the Retainer Liaison will confirm availability within 20 minutes.
- Shadowing: new oncall engineers must shadow three incident activations or two game days before solo paging.

Game day and rehearsal checklist (quarterly):
- Objectives: validate retainer engagement flow, practice cross-region failover, and evidence collection.
- Pre-game: pick a realistic scenario (KV corruption + noisy neighbor), identify participants and simulation window.
- Playbook: run full activation from alert -> bridge -> customer notice -> containment -> postmortem exercise.
- Scoring: measure time to bridge (target < 5m), time to mitigation (target < 20m), and evidence completeness (target 90%).
- After-action: publish lessons and update this runbook within 7 days.

Operational templates and quick references (appendix)
- Incident channel name: INCIDENT-{YYYYMMDD}-{SERVICE}-{SEV}
- Bridge subject line: "INCIDENT {SERVICE} {SEV} — {short description}"
- Quick commands (attach outputs to channel):
  - monitoring snapshot: curl -s "https://monitoring-api.redwood.internal/query?service=$SERVICE&window=15m" > incident-metrics.json
  - get deployment history: git log --pretty=format:'%h %s' --since='24 hours' services/$SERVICE

- Minimal evidence export checklist (for billing/retainer reconciliation):
  | item | why | owner | deadline |
  |-----|-----|------|---------|
  | metrics-15m.json | shows SLO breach window | SRE Lead | +1 hour |
  | logs-archive.tgz | correlated requests | SRE Lead | +4 hours |
  | deployment-commits.txt | links to potential regressions | Release Eng | +24 hours |
  | customer-impact.csv | list of affected tenants | Customer Liaison | +2 hours |

Governance and continuous improvement:
- This document is reviewed quarterly by Engineering, CS, and Legal.
- Any changes to activation criteria must be approved by SRE and the Head of Product.
- Track improvements as action items on the incident ticket and include owner and due date.

Related references:
- See also: Incident command playbook and escalation matrix (internal link), Incident evidence chain and forensic runbook (internal link).

Contact matrix (primary contacts):
- IC rotation: ic-rotation@redwood.internal
- Bridge Operator oncall: bridge-oncall@redwood.internal
- Retainer Liaison: retainer-liaison@redwood.internal

Notes:
- Keep communications factual; avoid speculation about root cause until confirmed.
- Preserve all evidence in the incident tracker for at least 180 days to support contractual or regulatory needs.
